questions.en: Explain with example the writing of physical quantities into their dimensions. Write the two benefits.

Astronomers usually measure astronomical distance in light years. One light year is the distance that light travel in one year. If speed of light is 3x10<sup>8</sup>ms<sup>-1</sup>, what is one light year in metres?
Write the estimated answer of the following in standard form. (a) How many second are there in 1 year? (b) How many years are in 1 second?
What is meant by uncertainty 1n a measurement? How the uncertainty in a digital instrument is indicated?
The mass of solid cylinder is 12.85 g. Its length is 3.35 cm and diameter is 1.25 cm. Find the density of its material expressing the uncertainty in the density.

Derive a formula for the period of a simple pendulum using dimensional analysis. The various possible factors on which the time period T may depend are: (i) length of the pendulum (ii) Mass of the bob m (iii) angle which the thread makes with the vertical (iv) acceleration due to gravity g.
What is meant by signigicant figures? write two reasons for using them in measurements. How to find the uncertainty in a timing experiment such as the time period of a simple pendulum?
The length and width of a rectangular plate are measured to be 18.3 cm and 14.60 cm, respectively. Find the area of the plate and state the answer to correct number of significant figures.
Differentiate between the terms precision and accuracy with reference to measurement of physical quantities.
The diameter and length of a metal cylinder measured with the help of a Vernier Callipers of least count 0.01 cm are 1.22 cm and 5.35 cm respectively. Calculate its volume and uncertainty in it.
Check the homogeneity of the relation . where v is the speed of transverse wave of a stretched string of tension T, length l and mass m.

Show that the expression is dimensionally correct, where v is the initial velocity. a is the acceleration and Vf is the velocity after covering a distance S. Show that the famous "Einstein equation E=mc2 is dimensionally consistent.
Show that the famous "Einstein equation E=mc<sup>2</sup> is dimensionally consistent.
Define and explain scalar product. Write down its important characteristics.
Define and explain vector product of two vectors. Discuss important characteristics of vector product.
The magnitude of cross and scalar products of two vectors are , respectively. Find the angle between the vectors.
If IA+BI = IA-BI, then prove that A and B are perpendicular to each other.
Derive three equations of motion by graphical method.
A helicopter is ascending vertically at the rate of 19.6 m s<sup>-1</sup>. When it is at a height of 156.8 m above the ground, a stone is dropped. How long does the stone take to reach the ground?
What is projectile motion? Explain.
Derive the following expressions for projectile motion: (i) time of flight (ii) height attained (iii) range for projectile.
A cricket ball is hit upward with velocity of 20 m s<sup>-1</sup> at an angle of 45<sup>o</sup> with the ground. Find its: (a) time of flight (b) maximum height (c) how far away it hits the ground.
An aeroplane is moving horizontally at a speed of 200 ms<sup>-1</sup> at a height of 8 km to drop a bomb on a target. Find horizontal distance from the target at which the bomb should be released.

Why does range R of a projectile remain the same when angle of projection is changed from 0 to 0' = 90<sup>o</sup> - 0. Also show that for complementary angles of projection, the ration R/R' is equal to 1.

A body of mass M at  rest explodes into 3 pieces, two of which of mass M / 4 each are thrown off in perpendicular directions with velocities of 3 m s<sup>-1</sup> and 4 m s<sup>-1</sup>, respectively. Find the velocity of 3<sup>rd</sup> piece with which it will be flown away.
A 20 g ball hits the wall of a squash court with a constant force of 50 N. If the time of impact of force is 0.50 s, Find the impulse.

A ball is kicked by a footballer. The average force on the ball is 240 N, and the impact lasts for a time interval of 0.25 s. (a) Calculate change on momentum (b) State the direction of change in momentum.

A trolley of mass 1.0 kg moving with velocity 1.0 ms<sup>-1</sup> collides with a similar trolley at rest: (i) after collision, the 1<sup>st</sup> trolley comes to rest whereas the second starts moving with velocity of 1.0 m s<sup>-1</sup> in the same direction. Show that it is an example of an elastic collision. (ii) After the collision, they stick together and move away with a velocity of 0.5 ms<sup>-1</sup>. Show that it is an example of an inelastic collision.
Explain elastic collision in one dimension. Show that magnitude of relative velocities before and after collision are equal.
Explain an inelastic collision in one dimensions.

A railway wagon of mass 4 x 10<sup>4</sup> kg moving with velocity of 3 ms<sup>-1</sup> collides with another wagon of mass 2 x 10<sup>4</sup> kg which is at rest. They stick together and more off together. Find their combined velocity.
Explain elastic collision in two dimensions.

A car with mass 575 kg moves at 15.0 ms<sup>-1</sup> smashes into the rear end of a car with mass 1575 kg moves at 5 ms<sup>-1</sup> in the same direction. (a) what is the final velocity if the wrecked car lock together? (b) How much kinetic energy is lost in the collision?
Prove that (i)   (ii)

A laser beam is directed from the Earth to the Moon. If the beam is to have a diameter of 2.50 m at the Moon, how small must divergence angle be for the beam? The distance of Moon from the Earth is 3.8 x 10<sup>8</sup>m.
A car is moving with a speed of 108 km h<sup>-1</sup>. If its wheel has diameter of 60 cm, find its angular speed in rad s<sup>-1</sup> and rev s<sup>-1</sup>.
An electric motor is running at 1800 rev min<sup>-1</sup>. On switching off, it comes to rest in 20 s. If angular retardation is uniform. Find the number of revolutions it makes before stopping.
A string 0.5 m long holding a stone can withstand maximum tension of 35.6 N, Find the maximum speed at which a stone of 0.5 kg mass can be whirled with it in a vertical circle.
What are artificial satellites? Calculate the minimum time period necessary to put a satellite into the orbit near the surface of the Earth.
Define orbital velocity and derive an expression for the same.
Write a note of artificial gravity. Derive an expression for frequency with which the spaceship rotate to provide artificial gravity.
A satellite is orbiting the Earth at an altitude of 200 km. Assuming the Earth's radius is 6400 km. Calculate the orbital speed of the satellite.
A space station has a radius of 20 m and rotates at an angular velocity of 0.5 rad s<sup>-1</sup>. What is the artificial gravity experienced by the astronauts on the space station?
Define moment of inertia. Prove that torque acting on rotating rigid body is equal to the product of its moment of inertia and angular acceleration.

The flywheel of an engine is rotating at 2100 rev min<sup>-1</sup> when the power source is shut off. What torque is required to stop it in 3 minutes? The moment of inertia of the flywheel is 36 kg m<sup>2</sup>.
What is the moment of inertia of a 200 kg sphere whose diameter is 60 cm?
A bicycle wheel has an angular momentum of 10 kg m<sup>2</sup> s<sup>-1</sup> and angular velocity of 2 rad s<sup>-1</sup> Find the value of its moment of inertia.
What is meant by angular momentum? Explain the law of conservation of angular momentum with daily life examples.
Show that orbital angular momentum is .

A diver comes off a board with arms straight up and legs straight down, giving him a moment of inertia of 18 kg m<sup>2</sup> about his rotation axis. Then tucks into a small ball. decreasing his moment of inertia to 3.6 kg m<sup>2</sup>. While tucked, he makes two complete rotations in 1.0 seconds. If he had not tucked at all, how many revolutions would he have made in 1.5 s from board to water?

An electrical motor of one horse power is used to run a water pump. water pump takes 15 minutes to fill a tank of 400 litres at a height of 10 m (1 hp 746 watts). Find: (a) actual input work done by electric motor to fill the tank (b) actual output work done.
How is work done by a: (i) constant force (ii) variable force?

If an object of mass 2 kg thrown up from ground reaches a height of 5 m and flashback to the Earth (neglecting air resistance), calculate: (i) work done by gravity when the object reaches at 5 m height. (ii) work done by gravity when the object comes back to the Earth (iii) total work done by gravity in upward and downward motion. Also mention physical significance of the result.

A passenger just arrives at the airport and dragging his suitcase to luggage check in at the desk. He pulls strap with a force of 200 N at an angle of 45<sup>o</sup> to the floor to displace it 50 m to the desk. Determine the value of work done by him on the suitcase.
Define conservative field. Show that gravitational field is conservative in nature.
An object weighing 98 N is dropped from a height of 10 m. Its speed just before hitting the ground is 12 ms<sup>-1</sup>. What is the frictional force acting on it?
A machine gun is fires 6 bullets per minute with a velocity of 700 ms<sup>-1</sup>. If each bullet has a mass of 40 g. then find power developed by the gun?
Define K.E and derive an expression for the same.
What is meant by absolute P.E? Derive an expression for absolute P.E.

Define escape velocity. Show that an expression for escape velocity can be expressed as , where R and g denote radius of the Earth and acceleration due to gravity, respectively. Also find its numerical value near the surface of the Earth.
A 1200 kg car is running at a speed of 40 km h<sup>-1</sup>. How much power will be expended by it to accelerate at 2 ms<sup>-2</sup>.

A 200 g apple is lifted to 10 m and then dropped. What is the its velocity when it hits the ground? Assume that 75% of work done in lifting the apple if transferred to K.E by the time it hits the ground.
State and explain work-energy theorem in a resistive medium.

A family uses of 10 kW of power. Direct solar energy is incident on horizontal surface at an average rate of 300 W per square metre. If 75% of this energy can be converted into needed to supply 10 kW?
The mass of the Earth is 6.0 x 10<sup>24</sup> kg and mass of the Sun is 1.99 x 10<sup>30</sup> kg. The Sun is 160 million km away from the Earth. Find the value of gravitational P.E of the Earth.
A 75 watt fan is used for 8 hours daily fro 30 day. Find: (i) Energy consumed in electrical units. (ii) Electricity bill if one unit costs Rs. 22.5?
Explain in detail the classification of solids with respect to atomic arrangements.

A copper wire of length 3 metres and cross-sectional area of 1 x 10<sup>-6</sup> m<sup>2</sup> is subjected to a force of 500 N. Calculate the stress and strain produced in the wire. (Young;s modulus of copper Y = 1.1 x 10<sup>11</sup> Nm<sup>-6</sup>).

A steel wire of length 2 metres and cross-sectional area of 2 x 10<sup>-6</sup> m<sup>2</sup> by a force of 400 N. If the Young's modulus of steel is 2 x 10<sup>11</sup> Nm<sup>-2</sup>, calculate the extension of the wire.
A spring with spring constant 200 N m<sup>-1</sup> is stretched by 0.5 m. Find the elastic P.E. stored in the spring.
What is Archimedes principle? Explain it in detail for finding upthrust.
A block of wood of mass 10 kg and density of 600 kg m<sup>-3</sup> floating in water. Calculate the buoyant force acting on the block. (Density of water = 1000 kg m<sup>-3</sup>).
Justify that mass remains conserved when a fluid flows through a pipe.
State and derive equation of continuity.
State and prove Bernoulli's equation.
Give some practical applications of Bernoulli's equation.

Water flows through a horizontal pipe with a velocity of 3 ms<sup>-1</sup> and pressure of 200,000 pa at point 1. At the nozzle (point 2), the pressure decreases to atmospheric pressure 101,300 pa and the velocity increases to 14 ms<sup>-1</sup>. Calculate the velocity of the water exiting the nozzle.
A tank filled with water has a hole at a depth of 5 m from the water surface. Calculate the velocity of water flowing out of the hole.
Define terminal velocity of a body and show that terminal velocity is directly proportional to the square of radius of the body.
Water flows through a pipe with a diameter of 0.05 m at a velocity of 2 ms<sup>-1</sup>. If the pipe narrows to a diameter of 0.03 m. Calculate the velocity of water at narrow section.

Calculate the terminal velocity of a spherical raindrop with a radius 0.5 mm falling through the air. (7 for air = 19 x 10<sup>-6</sup>kg m<sup>-1</sup>s<sup>-1</sup>, p=1000 kg m<sup>-3</sup> for water).
Explain the term of superfluidity.

State and explain various gas laws.
A gas occupies 60. L of volume at a pressure of 12 atm. What will be the volume of gas if the pressure is increased by 2.0 atm, assuming that temperature remains constant?

In a vacuum chamber which is connected to a cryogenic pump, pressure as low as 1,00 npa is being attained. Calculate the number of molecules in 1.00 m<sup>3</sup> vessel at this pressure and temperature of 300 K.
A gas occupies 400 mL at 20<sup>o</sup>C. What volume will it occupy at 80<sup>o</sup>C, assuming constant pressure?
A gas has pressure of 2 atm at 300 K. What pressure will it have at 450 K, assuming constant volume.
Explain first law of thermodynamics in detail. Give an example in support to your explanation. Give its two applications.

What is Carnot engine? Describe Carnot cycle. State Carnot theorem and derive an expression for efficiency of Carnot engine.

A Carnot engine is operating between a high temperature reservoir at 600 k and a low temperature reservoir at 300 K. Calculate: (i) the maximum possible efficiency  (ii) the amount of work output if the engine absorb 500 j of heat from the high temperature reservoir.
What is refrigerator? Explain it working. Derive an expression for its coefficient of performance.

A refrigerator extracts 1200 j of heat from its interior (the cold reservoir) and release 1800 j of heat to the surrounding environment (the hot reservoir) during each cycle. Calculate: (i) the work input required per cycle (ii) the coefficient of performance (COP) of the refrigerator.
Define and explain the term "Entropy".
Calculate the entropy change when 1.0 moles of ice at 0<sup>o</sup>C melts from liquid water at the same temperature . (Heat of fusion of ice per mole= 6.01x10<sup>3</sup> j).

What is meant by the term beats? Prove that number of beats per second is equal to the difference between the frequencies of vibrating tuning forks.
